advisory.finding: Removing the verify_opcert call eliminates ALL DSSE signature verification (including the Phase 0 subject-binding / replay defense), not just the source-of-certification gating the ticket intended to drop. opcert_from_record only DECODES the envelope; nothing now verifies the signature is valid, yet the gate hardcodes 'verified': True and trusts the decoded payload's material_fingerprint/merged_log_commit/manifest.
merged_from: The bugfix-size attestation gate no longer cryptographically verifies the plan-review op-cert's DSSE signature: `classify_plan_review_attestation` parses the envelope (`opcert_from_record` only calls `dsse.decode`/`json.loads`) and then hardcodes `{'opcert': True, 'verified': True}` into the dict fed to `compute_validity`, so any decodable envelope is treated as signature-verified. Because the attestation record lives on the auto-pushed, non-Gerrit-gated tickets branch (documented attacker-writable), an actor who can write that branch can fabricate a well-formed envelope with any (or an invalid) signature and satisfy the gate — the signature is never checked.

advisory.finding: Removing `verify_opcert` also drops its Phase-0 subject-binding check (ticket_id / material_fingerprint / merged_log_commit / kind digest), which was the cross-ticket/cross-material replay defense. In the new path, `compute_validity` reads `ticket_id` implicitly (via the ticket-keyed record) and `material_fingerprint`/`merged_log_commit` from the UNVERIFIED envelope payload, then compares them against current ticket state. An attacker crafting a record can set the payload's `material_fingerprint` to the value the current material computes to, so the `stale-material` check will not fire and a genuine other-ticket review (or a hand-crafted one) can be replayed onto the target bug.
